title: Checkout identity survives an rm -rf and re-clone on an inode-reusing filesystem
description: Found by the Opus review of opum-ai/ward-cli#237 (WCLI-99, APPROVE, finding 1, MEDIUM, product). A checkout is identified only by (root, device, inode): src/adapters/checkout.ts builds the identity, findBinding matches on it in src/domain/vault-state.ts, profile approvals match the same tuple, and unregister.ts and reporting.ts match it too. On a filesystem that reuses a freed inode, a checkout deleted with rm -rf and re-cloned at the same path gets the same identity and silently inherits the old binding and every profile approval. That breaks spec section 7.1, which requires a new clone to be handled explicitly, and the comment in vault-state.ts claims exactly that guarantee. Evidence: the hosted ext4 runner in #237 reproduced it (project-binding T10, now moved aside in the test so it no longer reuses the inode). APFS rarely reuses inode numbers, so the macOS preview is mostly unaffected. ADR 0004 commits to Linux (WCLI-21) and Windows (WCLI-22), so this blocks the Linux T26 run. Needs a design decision from the operator via opum-doc (what else identifies a clone: a creation time, a nonce written into .ward at registration, or the .git directory identity) before it is built.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision on what identifies a checkout beyond (root, device, inode) is recorded by opum-doc and as an ADR here

On a filesystem that reuses a freed inode, rm -rf of a registered checkout and a re-clone at the same path is treated as a new checkout: no inherited binding and no inherited profile approval, with a test that does not move the old directory aside
WCLI-21 lists this task as a dependency of its T26 run

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-11-03 to DEC-255 (a2)(4) and (a6), as relayed verbatim by the leader (record: opum-doc, DEC-255 outcome (a6), opum-ai/opum-doc#1597). ADR 0026 names both, supersedes the identity part of ADR 0005 and amends ADR 0023 (the supersede/amend banners on 0005 and 0023 were left out because the shared agent-profile budgets in .lore/agents were already at their limit; 0026's Status names both).

What changed: sameCheckout in src/domain/vault-state.ts now requires root, device, inode AND a present, equal checkoutId; findBinding, isApprovalFor (profile approvals), unregister's belongsTo and withoutBinding, and doctor's stale-approval probe all go through it or compare the nonce. checkoutId is the one optional key on binding and approval records (reader and serializer; absent is omitted, never null; vaultStateFormatVersion stays 1). src/adapters/checkout.ts reads and, after an approved registration only, creates $GIT_DIR/ward/checkout-id (exclusive create, 0600, refusing links; a .git file's gitdir: line read as one bounded 4 KiB line, relative paths against the .git file's directory, realpath, existing directory; GIT_DIR env never read). A git directory that cannot be resolved or written refuses registration with the new catalog code checkout_identity_unavailable. initProject takes a bindCheckout port, wired in src/cli/main.ts.

Evidence: bun run check green, 1172 pass. test/checkout-identity.test.ts pins identical (root, device, inode) with another nonce as a new checkout for bindings and approvals, the optional-key reader and serializer, and the file rules; test/project-binding.test.ts adds an rm -rf and re-clone at the same path (no move aside). Mutation: making sameCheckout ignore the nonce turns the two domain cases red. On APFS the e2e re-clone case still gets a different inode, so it stays green under that mutation; the nonce guarantee is carried by the domain cases, not by the platform's inode behaviour. Not measured: a filesystem that actually reuses the inode (Linux T26 is the first such run; this task is not a flip gate).

Consequences carried for the next release (release path not edited): the release notes of the next release need one line, "a vault written by this version carries a new optional record key, so a 0.1.1 binary refuses it as malformed; downgrade to 0.1.1 is unsupported" (DEC-255 a6 Q1). Existing 0.1.1 bindings and approvals read as unbound and stay in the vault inert; a legacy binding cannot be unregistered from its checkout. The existing profile-approval re-approval filter does not replace a legacy approval (it has no nonce), so it remains inert beside the new one.

CORRECTION under DEC-255 (a7) (opum-doc origin/dev 8e1a5e4, opum-ai/opum-doc#1601, text as relayed by the leader; it supersedes the legacy-record consequences in the build note above, whose last sentence said a legacy binding cannot be unregistered and a legacy approval is not replaced). (a7) accepts checkout_identity_unavailable, and rules that legacy (0.1.1, no checkoutId) records still never match for authorization but can be removed: ward unregister, run in a checkout, also removes a legacy binding at the same (root, device, inode) together with that binding's legacy approvals (under the same two questions; a declined first question changes nothing), and approving a profile also removes a legacy approval for the same profile and directory so the new record replaces it. Records nobody touches stay inert; no doctor or cleanup command is filed. Built as new commits on #254: legacyBindingsAt and isReplacedBy in src/domain/vault-state.ts, runUnregister in src/application/unregister.ts. Tests: test/unregister.test.ts (legacy-only cleared with its approvals and still denied after; a declined unregister leaves the vault byte-identical; a legacy binding beside a current one is cleared with it, the other checkout untouched) and test/checkout-identity.test.ts (a legacy approval matches nothing with or without a nonce; approving removes only the same profile and directory, keeping other profiles, directories and another clone's approval; a legacy record never authorizes before or after). Mutation controls, each run and restored: letting a missing nonce match turns four cases red (the legacy-never-matches cases and the legacy unregister case); removing the approve-side legacy branch turns two red; making unregister ignore legacy bindings turns two red. ADR 0026 now names (a7) and states the APFS limit (the e2e re-clone gets a new inode there, so the domain cases carry the guarantee and real reuse is first measured on Linux T26).

Opus review of opum-ai/ward-cli#254 recorded as written. Unit: ward-cli-review-254 (transcript model claude-opus-5-5 on all 42 turns, per the leader). Head: 06dad7a. Worktree: review-254-06dad7a. The verdict covers 06dad7a and predates the (a7) commit 6022327.

VERDICT: APPROVE (opum-ai/ward-cli#254, WCLI-125). Nothing blocks; the findings below are LOW or NIT follow-ups.
HEAD: 06dad7a

Checked and clean:
- (1) Every site that grants or keeps authority goes through sameCheckout, which requires a present and equal nonce: findBinding, isApprovalFor (and so findProfileApproval, withProfileApproval and withoutProfileApproval), requireBinding/bindingNaming in binding.ts, run.ts, and profiles approve/revoke. unregister's belongsTo/withoutBinding and the doctor's stale probe compare the nonce inline. Grepping `.inode` across src finds no comparison on the tuple alone.
- (2) checkoutId is the only optional key. It must match /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/; null, uppercase and malformed values refuse the document. An absent key is omitted, never written as null, in bindings, approvals and the stale passthrough. Unknown and missing keys still refuse. formatVersion stays 1. As the advisor asked, I read parseVaultState in full: there is no uniqueness rule keyed on the tuple, and no count cap on bindings or approvals (only auditHistoryLimit). So the legacy record and the new record sharing one tuple after an upgrade does not brick the vault.
- (3) The nonce comes from randomBytes(16) as hex. It is written only inside registerForProject, which runs only on an "approved" answer. It is never in .ward, and no output or audit field carries it (grepped).
- (4) Only the `.git` entry the root walk found is followed, and GIT_DIR is never read. The `.git` file is read with O_NOFOLLOW, at most 4 KiB. One trailing LF or CRLF is stripped; any other CR, LF or NUL is refused, as is a missing prefix or an empty path. A relative path resolves against the root, which is the directory holding the file. The target goes through realpath and must be a directory. The file is created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW at 0600, and the ward directory at 0700 with a lstat check.
- (5) A linked worktree's pointer names its own .git/worktrees/<n>, so each worktree gets its own nonce.
- (6) ADR 0026 names DEC-255 (a2)(4) and (a6), the §7.1 exception, that it supersedes the identity part of 0005, and that it amends 0023.
- AC3 already holds: WCLI-21's dependencies are ["WCLI-5","WCLI-125"].
- checkout_identity_unavailable is sound on its merits. It fails closed, binds nothing, and sits after approval.

FINDINGS:
1. LOW. docs/adr/0026-a-checkout-is-identified-by-its-directory-identity-and-a-nonce-in-its-git-directory.md, Consequences, second bullet. The ADR says an inert record stays "until the checkout is unregistered or re-approved with the same identity", and that "ward doctor names a stale approval it cannot match". Both are false for a 0.1.1 legacy record:
   - withoutBinding keeps it, because `undefined !== nonce`.
   - withProfileApproval never matches it.
   - No command can ever remove it.
   - The doctor covers only version-stale approvals. It mislabels a legacy one as "a different directory now stands at that path" (src/application/reporting.ts:416-422), or as "no longer registered" when neither side has a nonce.
   - Current-version 0.1.1 approvals that went inert are not reported anywhere.
   The task's implementation notes say this correctly; the binding ADR does not. Why it matters: the ADR is the record a later reader trusts.
2. LOW. src/adapters/checkout.ts:294-305 (bindCheckoutIdentity) and 136-145 (readCheckoutId). Time-of-check to time-of-use: O_NOFOLLOW guards only the final component. If the `ward` directory is swapped for a link between `lstatSync(directory)` and `openSync(file, …)`, the create is redirected. The same gap applies to the realpath'd gitdir before use. It needs a concurrent process under the same account, which is outside ADR 0002, and the payload is a harmless nonce. Still, "refusing symlinks at both" holds only at check time. Name it in the ADR residual, or open the directory with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW where the runtime allows.
3. LOW. Tests: the mutation claim is true but narrower than it reads. Making sameCheckout ignore the nonce does turn the two domain cases in test/checkout-identity.test.ts red. The inline nonce comparisons in unregister.ts:61 and :77 and reporting.ts:420 have no test that fails if they are dropped. Each of them only narrows removal or diagnosis, so no authority leaks.
   Also missing:
   - no test registers twice at one identical tuple and round-trips that through serialize and parse (the upgrade path);
   - the e2e re-clone case in test/project-binding.test.ts checks the binding but not profile approvals (AC2 is met only in combination with the domain test);
   - there are no CRLF, NUL, missing-trailing-newline, `../` relative or symlinked-gitdir pointer cases.
4. LOW, residual. A submodule's git directory lives in the superproject's .git/modules/<n>, and a linked worktree's in .git/worktrees/<n>. Both survive an `rm -rf` of the working directory. A `git submodule update` re-populates from the surviving git directory and keeps the nonce, so on a filesystem that reuses inodes the binding and approvals carry over. This complies with "the clone's git dir", but ADR 0026's residual should say so.
5. LOW. ADRs 0005 and 0023 carry no supersede or amend note, even though ADRs 0010 and 0018 set the precedent of in-file amendment notes. The reason given is the agent-profile token budget. Separately, .lore/agents/review.toml drops 0005 entirely, so reviewers also lose the parts of 0005 that this change does not supersede.
6. NIT. src/contract/errors.ts:197-202. A damaged or empty checkout-id is a permanent dead end. That includes a crash between the exclusive create and the write, and a concurrent registration reading the file before the writer has written it. The hint never says to remove `<gitdir>/ward/checkout-id`.
7. NIT. Stale comments:
   - vault-state.ts:1148-1151 still says "All four parts … project, root, device, inode".
   - project-binding.test.ts, the re-clone test comment, says "nor, once registered again, a binding for the old clone", which is garbled.
   - project.ts:155 writes the nonce before the binding_conflict check. That is harmless, but the "written at binding time" comment overstates it.
8. NIT. The PR's size (772 added lines) hides nothing. Most of it is test fixtures gaining checkoutId and the new test file.

UNVERIFIED:
- That `bun run check` passes (1172 tests) and that the mutation run behaves as claimed. I have no shell; I confirmed the mutation logic only by reading.
- Behaviour on a filesystem that actually reuses inodes (Linux T26).
- Whether `git worktree add -f` at a stale registered path reuses the old .git/worktrees/<n> directory, and so the old nonce.
- The opum-doc text of DEC-255 itself. I compared against the verbatim relay in the brief, not the record.
